intended_object: The surjective restriction map O(GL_n) → O(U_n) = O(GL_n)/I, where I is the ideal generated by the entries below the diagonal and by the diagonal entries minus 1. It is the comorphism of the closed immersion of the upper-unitriangular group U_n into GL_n (Milne 2.9). Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and how the file uses the map.
explanation:
The body is `Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ K (ideal K ι)`, the canonical K-algebra surjection onto the quotient. The ring being quotiented is the determinant-localized coordinate ring of GL_ι over K. `ideal` is spanned by `relation i j`: x_ij when j < i, x_ii − 1 on the diagonal, and 0 otherwise. These are exactly the equations cutting out the upper-unitriangular matrices, so the quotient is the coordinate ring of U_n. The file goes on to prove that the ideal is a Hopf ideal and that the quotient is the polynomial ring on the strictly upper entries. Both results confirm that this is the right object.

The generality is natural. K is any commutative ring (no field or flatness is assumed), and ι is any finite linearly ordered index type, which the notion of "upper triangular" needs. Requiring ι and K to live in the same universe is a minor technical restriction inherited from the library's GL construction, not a mathematical narrowing.

Mathlib has no coordinate ring of U_n and no such quotient map, so there is no counterpart. The definition is the standard quotient map and adds nothing extra.
